data.body:
CORRECTION to the prior comment — I overstated this. It is NOT "blocking all Gerrit landings."

Empirical evidence (2026-08-04 ~20:37 UTC): changes are landing normally — 1387, 1378, 1379 all
merged within minutes, and gerrit-verify runs 30945952757 / 30946364334 were SUCCESS.

What actually happens: the "filtered tickets pack exceeds its limit" step (limit 131072 KiB) trips
only for changes on a STALE BASE (a merge preview several commits behind origin/main carries more
delta ticket-event objects, inflating the filtered pack past the threshold). Changes freshly based
on current origin/main pass it. Proven both ways on the same ticket:
  - 1376 PS3 (base 7 commits stale) -> pack step FAILED (131431 KiB > 131072).
  - 1376 PS4 (rebased onto current main) -> Verified +1 SUCCESS.
  - 1386 PS3 (stale base) -> same pack step FAILED; remedy is the same rebase.

So this is a marginal-threshold gate, not a global block. Corrected scope for this ticket: the
filtered pack is close enough to 128 MiB that stale-based changes keep tripping it, so proactive
tickets-branch repack/gc (this ticket's maintenance scope) is still worthwhile to add headroom and
stop the recurring stale-base failures — but it is NOT on the critical path and does not gate
current-main-based landings. Downgrading from "URGENT/critical-path" to "worthwhile maintenance".
